Thanks — adding technical notes ahead of the shiproom. See attached minimal schema and a short ops diff. High-level:
- Fallback behavior: we will attempt primary vector DB (pgvector or Pinecone) with a 150ms per-request target. If the DB does not acknowledge within 300ms or error rate > 1% for a 1m window, requests will be routed to the S3 cold-lane retriever (batched KV lookup + unstructured re-rank).
- Circuit breaker: incremental backoff + sample-based QA gate before full fallthrough.
- Test vectors: please include three load profiles: normal (1k qps sustained), spike (5k qps 30s), and recovery (gradual downscale).
- Observability: we'll instrument token-level latency, vector DB TTL misses, and cache hit-rate. Ben will share concrete queries.

Attaching: test_index_schema_v1.json (sample fields + embed dims), ops-runbook-diff.txt (what changes when fallthrough is enabled).

-rishi

Thanks everyone — confirming we got the attachments and the agenda. A few clarifications before the 3pm shiproom:
- Arcadia can run the indexing script to a Pinecone sandbox, but prefer Redwood to host the S3 test bucket so we can validate fallthrough behavior end-to-end. Can you share bucket details and minimal IAM perms?
- For the partial-document retrieval case, we'll provide labeled examples; could we also get a sample re-rank threshold (e.g., top-10 re-rank window) that Redwood uses so our model aligns?
- On retention: Arcadia's default is 90 days for intermediate vectors; we need to understand Redwood's retention guarantees for cold-tier mirrors before finalizing.

Maya and I will join from our product + infra chairs and bring a short list of test vectors. See you shortly.

—Tom
